ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, officers, shareholders holding 10% or more, authorized signatories, and clients against (i) the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List maintained under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act, as administered by Global Affairs Canada; (ii) the United States OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) List; (iii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; and (iv) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List. Politically exposed persons (PEPs) and heads of international organizations must be identified using the FINTRAC definition under the PCMLTFA and screened before engagement; enhanced due diligence and senior-management approval are mandatory for PEPs, foreign states ranked as High-Increase-Risk by FATF, and complex or opaque ownership structures.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry (Government of Alberta) at alberta.ca/corporate-registry; NUANS electronic name search through authorized registry service providers
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A corporate name must consist of a distinctive element, a descriptive element and a mandatory legal element ('Limited', 'Incorporated', 'Corporation' or their abbreviations 'Ltd.', 'Inc.', 'Corp.'). Names may be in English, French, or a combination of both; names in any other script (Cyrillic, CJK, Arabic, etc.) require a Latin-alphabet transliteration and must not be confusingly similar to alphabetically searchable names in the NUANS database. Numerals may be used; a corporation may adopt a numbered name (e.g., 1234567 Alberta Ltd.) if the proposed word name is rejected or if no name clearance is sought.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Trust, Trust Company, Insurance, Assurant, Loan Corporation (prior approval of the provincial Superintendent of Financial Institutions required)
Attorney, Lawyer, Barrister, Solicitor, Legal Counsel (Law Society of Alberta approval required)
University, College, Institute of Technology (Campus Alberta post-secondary authorization required)
Engineer, Engineering, Consulting Engineer (APEGA approval required)
Physician, Doctor, Clinic, Medical, Surgical (professional medical college approval required)
Financial, Securities, Broker, Investment, Hedge Fund, Asset Management (Alberta Securities Commission and financial-services regulator approval required)
Royal, Crown, Government, RCMP, Police (prior federal/provincial Crown authorization required)
Chartered Professional Accountant, CPA, Auditing (CPA Alberta authorization required for representational use)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection by the Alberta Corporate Registry, the applicant may (1) request a fresh NUANS search and file an amended incorporation application through an authorized registry service provider; (2) within 30 days of refusal, submit a written administrative reconsideration to the Director, Alberta Corporate Registry, attaching evidence of market distinctiveness, trademark-likelihood analysis, or a notarized consent letter from the conflicting nameholder; (3) if the conflict is trademark-based, obtain a consent-to-use or coexistence agreement from the mark owner; (4) if administrative reconsideration fails, incorporate under a numbered name (e.g., 1234567 Alberta Ltd.) and register an assumed business name (trade style) under the Alberta Business Names Registration Act, R.S.A. 2000, c. B-6, or (5) commence judicial review at the Alberta Court of King's Bench on grounds of procedural unfairness.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for this industry. The Alberta Business Corporations Act requires a registered office situated in Alberta at a physical street address where process can be served; a post office box alone is prohibited. A licensed corporate registered-office provider or virtual-office suite in Calgary or Edmonton satisfies the statute. For an ISIC 6920 fractional CFO consultancy there is no provincial requirement for physical premises or local staff; operations may be fully remote so long as CRA records, GST/HST administration and the registered office record addresses are accurate and responsive.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (<5% annualized). CRA corporate and GST/HST examinations for advisory-service firms are predominantly documentary and conducted by correspondence or virtual interview; FINTRAC compliance examinations are directed mainly at money services businesses and high-risk reporting entities, not at registered low-risk accounting consultancy clients; municipal business licence spot-checks (Calgary/Edmonton) occur only on complaint or lottery and concern signage/occupancy, not remote operations.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Alberta), RSA 2000, c B-9, ss. 5-17 (incorporation), s. 10 (articles), s. 32(2) (bylaws), s. 106 (registered office)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) – Registry Agents Online (RAO)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital. Subscribed shares may be issued for any consideration determined by the directors. If subscription funds are paid before the corporate bank account is opened, the funds must be held by a director or solicitor in a trust or escrow account.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the corporation accept the subscriber's subscription for common shares and, upon receipt of the agreed consideration, the board ratifies the issuance of those shares; FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the corporation be established at [Address], [City], Alberta, and that the corporate counsel or authorized agent be directed to file the Notice of Registered Office with the Alberta Corporate Registry; FURTHER RESOLVED, that [Name] be appointed President, [Name] be appointed Secretary, and [Name] be appointed Chief Financial Officer (Virtual) with authority to open bank accounts, sign contracts, and complete ancillary statutory filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Search and Articles of Incorporation Preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry – accredited Registry Agent or RAO online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS name search to ensure the proposed corporate name is distinguishable and compliant. Prepare Form 1 Articles of Incorporation, specifying share structure, restrictions, and proposed registered office. Verify director eligibility and obtain each director's consent to act.
required_dossiers: Identification and residential addresses of all directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected by the Registrar, submit a revised name or file an application for reconsideration under the ABCA within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit Articles and Obtain Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) – RAO online filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the completed Form 1 electronically and pay the prescribed filing fee. The Registrar reviews the application and issues a Certificate of Incorporation, which establishes the corporation's legal existence under the ABCA.
required_dossiers: Proof of registered office and first directors
Any initial bylaw if adopted concurrently
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, file an amendment or supplementary information with the Corporate Registry within 30 days of the notice; an expedited resubmission can be made through a registry agent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt Organizational Bylaws and Appoint Officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors of the Corporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The initial directors adopt the corporation's organizational bylaws (quorum, fiscal year, meetings, indemnification) and pass the first board resolution contained in Section 1. The resolution ratifies share issuance, fixes the registered office, and appoints officers with delegated banking and contracting authority.
required_dossiers: Directors' written resolution (or waiver of notice)
Organizational bylaws signed by all directors
Minute book and corporate records binder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure any defect by executing a unanimous written resolution and filing it in the corporate records; if needed, amend the bylaws by subsequent board or shareholder resolution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issue Shares and File Registered Office Notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors and Alberta Corporate Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Issue share certificates to the subscriber(s) in accordance with the board resolution, record shareholdings in the register, and file Form 2 Notice of Registered Office with the Alberta Corporate Registry. Update the registered office if it changes from the one listed in the Articles.
required_dossiers: Director consent to act (or attached to Form 1)
Register of directors and share register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct any errors in the share register or registered office notice and refile online. Late corrections are handled by consent resolution and an amended Form 2.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and municipal business licensing department (e.g., City of Calgary Business Licensing, City of Edmonton licensing)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for a Business Number (BN) with CRA via the RC1 form; activate the GST/HST account, payroll deduction account (if applicable), and Alberta provincial corporate tax account. Apply with the municipal authority for a general business license covering a virtual CFO consultancy. If a commercial office is leased, obtain a fire and life safety inspection certificate and an Alberta OHS clearance for the premises.
required_dossiers: CRA RC1 – Request for a Business Number
Lease agreement or proof of home-office authorization
Alberta Fire Code inspection report (for commercial premises)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA requires further details, respond with director identification and proof of business address. For municipal license delays, request a temporary interim permit from the governing municipality and escalate through Alberta Business Link.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Municipal Business Licensing (City of Calgary / City of Edmonton) and Alberta Municipal Affairs – Business Link
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Municipal General Business License – Professional Services (Fractional CFO & Bookkeeping)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Non-industrial professional office use; no Environmental Impact Assessment report required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge. General municipal wastewater and stormwater bylaws apply; e-waste from electronics must be managed under the Alberta Recycling Regulation, and any non-hazardous office waste is subject to municipal collection requirements.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification required for any commercial office occupancy under the Alberta Fire Code (AR 155/2014). Structural load inspection required for leasehold improvements or mezzanine installations. Workplace compliance under the Alberta Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) Act and Code, including first-aid kit standards, ventilation, and ergonomic assessment for workstations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada; official digital portal: CRA My Business Account and GST/HST NETFILE (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html). Under the federal-provincial Tax Collection Agreement, CRA administers both federal Part I corporate income tax and Alberta provincial corporate income tax; Alberta Treasury Board and Finance is the provincial revenue authority responsible for Alberta-specific taxes (fuel, tobacco, etc.) but not corporate income tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign-owned Alberta-incorporated Business Corporation: (1) file Articles of Incorporation under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) or the Canada Business Corporations Act, maintaining a registered office in Alberta; (2) apply online or by Form RC1 for the 9-digit CRA Business Number (BN), which is the single statutory TIN for all federal and provincial tax programs; (3) activate the required program accounts during BN registration: RT (corporate income tax), GST/HST, RP (payroll if employees are hired), and RM (import/export if applicable); (4) disclose the full particulars of directors, officers, and the ultimate non-resident parent entity (if any) to CRA; (5) CRA issues the BN confirmation and creates a separately referenced GST/HST account number. A foreign entity with no Canadian presence that is required to register as a non-resident supplier must file RC1 under the non-resident GST/HST registrant stream, appoint a Canadian address for service/agent, and evidence its foreign registered address; (6) verify the GST/HST registration status of counterparties through CRA's public GST/HST Registry before issuing invoices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box pass-through election for corporations. Available statutory elections include: (i) Excise Tax Act s. 156 election among closely related corporations to deem intercompany taxable supplies made for nil consideration; (ii) s. 228(5)/(6) GST/HST return-period and annual-filing elections; (iii) CRA streamlined accounting credit election for non-resident registrants; (iv) Income Tax Act s. 111(4) election to waive the carry-back of taxable losses; (v) Part XIV branch tax elections applicable only to non-resident corporations. Hybrid mismatch rules (Income Tax Act ss. 18.2 and 18.3) apply automatically to deduction/non-inclusion and dual-inclusion mismatches and do not require an affirmative election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax). Alberta imposes no provincial retail sales tax and no provincial HST component, so the effective rate in Alberta is the 5% federal GST only, with a 0% provincial PST component.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 (small supplier threshold), measured on worldwide gross revenues from taxable supplies in the current calendar quarter and the four preceding calendar quarters. A non-resident supplier making taxable supplies in Canada must register for GST/HST once worldwide taxable revenues exceed CAD 30,000, unless all its Canadian supplies are zero-rated; a person may nevertheless register voluntarily. Registration is not required solely for exports or other zero-rated supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, CRA pre-approval of invoices, or digital stamping exists. CRA supports voluntary Pan-Canadian e-invoicing built on the PEPPOL interoperability framework. GST/HST returns and files must be transmitted electronically through GST/HST NETFILE or approved CRA application-to-application (API/SDK) channels. Registrants must retain electronic books and records for at least six years and make them available on CRA demand; invoices must contain the information prescribed by the GST/HST Input Tax Credit Information Regulations but require neither a QR code nor a government-issued fiscal stamp.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V, s. 6 (Excise Tax Act) when supplied for export and exported by the supplier or delivered to a common carrier/consignee for export before release from the supplier's custody; proof of actual removal from Canada is mandatory. Services (virtual CFO advisory, multi-currency ledger bookkeeping, outsourced financial management): zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V, s. 9 where the recipient is a non-resident who is not registered for GST/HST, the service does not relate to real property situated in Canada, tangible personal property situated in Canada at the time the service is performed, or intangible personal property intended for use principally in Canada. The supplier should obtain and retain a signed non-resident declaration evidencing the client's jurisdiction of organisation, foreign address, and non-registrant status, together with records showing the service was contracted by and delivered to the foreign person from abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration / Canada Export Report (AES/CAED or carrier-filed export report for goods exceeding CAD 2,000; retained as supporting evidence and not applicable to pure service exports)

Bill of Lading / Airway Bill / delivery receipt (for goods); for virtual CFO services, a signed services agreement, statement of work, and time-and-attendance log evidencing cross-border performance and delivery
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 / bank statement evidencing receipt of export proceeds from the non-resident purchaser in the agreed foreign currency or Canadian dollars
Non-resident status evidence pack: client certificate of good standing, foreign tax residency proof, and GST/HST non-registrant declaration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA export zero-rating verification reviews require reconstruction of the export evidence trail and reconciliation with bank remittances. On failure to substantiate zero-rating, CRA reverses the 0% rate, assesses uncollected GST output tax, disallows related input tax credits, and may impose: s. 280 failure-to-file penalties (1% of net tax plus 0.25% per full month up to 12 months); s. 285 gross negligence penalties of the greater of CAD 250 and 25% of the tax evaded; and prescribed interest. The normal GST/HST reassessment period is four years, extended to seven years for misrepresentation or neglect, and is unlimited in cases of fraud. Criminal prosecution under s. 327 of the Excise Tax Act may result in fines of up to 200% of the tax evaded and imprisonment for up to five years. Export receivables remaining unpaid beyond 180 days from invoicing trigger CRA audit scrutiny of revenue recognition and collection documentation, and may lead to adjustment of revenues and ITCs if the export is determined not to have been delivered to or paid by the non-resident purchaser.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), in conjunction with the Department of Finance Canada and the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI). Canada maintains no standalone Foreign Exchange Administration; currency, payments, and exchange-control powers are sourced from the Currency Act (R.S.C., 1985, c. C-52), the Bank of Canada Act, and the Bank Act (S.C. 1991, c. 46).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Alberta Annual Return (ARA) filed under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Service Alberta - Corporate Registry (Alberta Registrar of Corporations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 calendar days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation, amalgamation, or continuance; the registry issues a Notice of Annual Return showing the exact due date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file by the due date creates a default record and triggers warning notices; continued non-filing for an extended period (generally after one year of default) authorizes the Registrar to strike the corporation from the register through administrative dissolution. Restoration requires filing all outstanding annual returns and paying accrued reinstatement fees; after a prolonged period of dissolution, a court order may be required.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (federal income tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due no later than 6 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; any balance of tax is generally due within 2 months after year-end (3 months after year-end for an eligible Canadian-controlled private corporation).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty equal to 5% of the unpaid tax balance plus 1% per full month for up to 12 months, with additional repeated-failure penalties possible; daily statutory interest also accrues. CRA may direct the corporate registry to dissolve an inactive corporation failing to file for two consecutive years, and directors may be assessed for certain unremitted corporate tax liabilities.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Annual Return and Remittance (for annual filers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For annual filers, due within 3 months after the corporation's fiscal year-end; quarterly instalment payments apply where annual filing has been approved.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file penalty calculated at 1% of the net tax owing plus 25% of the assessed penalty amount remaining outstanding after 6 months; interest is compounded daily on unpaid amounts; directors and officers may be personally liable for knowingly unremitted GST/HST.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue or asset threshold in Alberta makes an audit compulsory for a private corporation. Under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), shareholders appoint an auditor each year unless all voting shareholders pass a unanimous resolution waiving the audit requirement. A certified audit becomes mandatory for a distributing corporation offering securities to the public, for corporations in regulated trust, insurance, or securities businesses, and where the Canada Revenue Agency, a creditor, or the shareholders require audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public enterprises and distributing corporations follow IFRS; private Canadian enterprises follow Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) under the CPA Canada Handbook. The virtual CFO and bookkeeping entity will normally prepare compiled or reviewed financial statements under ASPE and apply tax-basis adjustments for the federal T2 return.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta), the corporation must maintain an Individuals with Significant Control (ISC) register and record any change within 15 days of becoming aware. At each anniversary and annual-return cycle, directors must review share transfers, options, and control-in-fact arrangements from the preceding year, update or confirm the ISC register, and minute the confirmation at the annual meeting. Failure to prepare, maintain, or update the ISC register is an offence under the Alberta Business Corporations Act and may expose directors and the corporation to penalties.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 100 - 350 per year (CAD 135 - 470) for a standard Alberta registered office address and registered agent service; comprehensive corporate administration packages that include annual return calendar management and minute book maintenance generally range higher.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 - 20,000 (CAD 8,000 - 27,000) for a certified audit of the service corporation if audit is required; a review engagement, commonly used where the unanimous shareholder auditor waiver is in place, ranges approximately USD 3,500 - 8,000 (CAD 4,500 - 11,000).

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23.0% combined general corporate rate (Federal 15.0% + Alberta 8.0%); 11.0% combined (Federal 9.0% + Alberta 2.0%) on first CAD 500,000 of qualifying active business income for Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPC).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Small Business Deduction (CCPC only) reduces rate on first CAD 500,000; accelerated capital cost allowance deductions; Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credits; Foreign Tax Credit for foreign-source income; no statutory tax holidays in Alberta.
